extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing responses to peer review (researchers submitting manuscripts)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for authors on how to read, prioritize, and respond to peer-review reports and for reviewers/editors on judging a manuscript (status, accuracy, support, conclusions). Focuses on organization, professionalism, ethics, and practical revision tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer decision/status categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Alongside their report, reviewers assign a status to the article: Approved; Approved with reservations; Not approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions provided: Approved = scientifically sound in current form (only minor, if any, improvements suggested). Approved with reservations = a number of small changes, sometimes more significant revisions required to address specific details and improve academic merit. Not approved = fundamental flaws that seriously undermine findings and conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of topic in context of current literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the topic of the opinion/article discussed accurately in the context of the current literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should judge whether the manuscript situates its topic correctly with respect to recent and relevant literature; the example review marks this criterion 'Yes'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual correctness and citation support
rubrics_metrics.description: Are all factual statements correct and adequately supported by citations?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess that factual claims are accurate and that supporting citations are provided where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument support by published evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Are arguments sufficiently supported by evidence from the published literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether claims and arguments rely on and cite appropriate empirical or theoretical literature; reviewers in the example answered 'Yes'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance and justification of conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the conclusions drawn balanced and justified on the basis of the presented arguments?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conclusions should follow from the evidence and argumentation and not overreach; reviewers should mark whether conclusions are justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize feedback (major vs minor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categorize reviewer comments into major and minor critiques and focus on addressing major revisions first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advice: address issues that directly impact methodology, results, or conclusions before minor grammatical or stylistic fixes. Example: clarification of data analysis or adding experiments are major; grammar or stylistic edits are minor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete examples of major and minor comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide examples to distinguish major vs minor reviewer comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major examples: modifying central hypothesis, changing main algorithm, redoing an experiment. Minor examples: unclear statements, missing/incorrect references, unclear data presentation, grammatical concerns, adding an extra paragraph/table/figure, or an appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to every point / pay attention to details
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to every point raised by reviewers and document how each was addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a point-by-point response (often in a table) showing original comment, action taken, and location of change in manuscript. Attention to detail includes precise documentation of edits and explicit replies to each reviewer remark.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize responses clearly (use tables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize and present revisions and responses so reviewers and editors can easily follow what was changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The use of tables to map each reviewer comment to the authors' response and manuscript changes is recommended as an excellent, commonly advised method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain professionalism and constructive tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Be polite, respectful, and objective in responses; avoid personalizing critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should acknowledge reviewer input, express gratitude, and respond calmly and constructively, especially to challenging critiques. Practical phrasing examples provided (e.g., 'We thank the reviewer for their insightful feedback...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Express gratitude appropriately (avoid repetition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a well-crafted expression of thanks but avoid repetitive or excessive expressions of gratitude throughout the response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer suggested reducing repetitive focus on gratitude; one clear acknowledgement is usually sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek guidance when unsure
rubrics_metrics.description: If uncertain how to address a particular comment, consult the editor or a mentor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are encouraged to reach out to the editor in chief or a field-expert mentor to clarify ambiguous requests or to seek advice on handling difficult or contentious reviewer demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle reviewer requests that conflict with journal guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance respecting reviewer suggestions with adherence to the journal's guidelines and the authors' original vision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewer requests conflict with journal policies or the manuscript’s scope, seek editorial approval. Simplify recommendations and be explicit when asking an editor for a decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous and ethical situations — follow established guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow established ethical guidelines (e.g., COPE, ICMJE) and consult editors when facing ambiguous or potentially unethical situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: if reviewers ask not to cite specific authors for reputational reasons, contact the editor; if authors suspect a reviewer used AI-assisted technologies without disclosure, alert editors. Refer to COPE/ICMJE resources for concrete steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI tools for proofreading — use cautiously and as supplementary
rubrics_metrics.description: AI tools may help with proofreading but have limitations and should be used as a supplementary measure rather than a primary one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are advised to note that AI may miss linguistic nuances or contextual errors; rely on human review in addition to AI. A sentence was added recommending cautious use of AI tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid plagiarism of reviewers' comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not copy and paste reviewers' comments verbatim into the manuscript; instead paraphrase and integrate suggestions in your own words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit warning: copying reviewers' text into the manuscript can be viewed as a lack of originality or raise academic-integrity concerns. Paraphrase reviewer suggestions when incorporating them into the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge reviewers when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider formally acknowledging reviewers in the manuscript acknowledgements if their feedback substantially improved the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including reviewers in the acknowledgements (when their contributions were substantial) is suggested to recognize their role beyond the response letter; this fosters goodwill and recognizes reviewer labor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise workflow: documentation, communication, and final review
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a revision workflow that emphasizes clear documentation of changes, professional communication with editors/reviewers, and a careful final review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations include: keep clear records of edits, communicate requests to editors when necessary, and perform a final read-through (including checking for remaining errors and appropriate use of AI tools).
